subject: Batched inference failover carveout & credit tranche — SLA negotiation
messages:
From: Tom Hsu <ops@nebula.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <contracts@nebula.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA exception request — batched inference failover and credits

Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran a quick post-demo runbook with our infra team and identified one area that will need clarification before we move forward: our production workload relies heavily on large batched inference jobs and an active regional failover for DR. That changes how availability is measured for us (sustained throughput vs single-request latency).

Two asks from our side:
- A carveout in the SLA for scheduled regional failovers (we expect up to 6h/month during phased DR drills) so those windows don't trigger credits.
- A monthly credit structure that accounts for batch throughput degradation separately from per-request latency. Preferably a two-tranche approach: one tranche for availability (uptime) and one for degraded throughput (tokens/sec).

Priya is cc'd and will handle contract language once we have a proposal. Can you share a suggested amendment or a draft so our procurement team can review?

Appreciate it,
Tom Hsu
Head of Platform Operations
Nebula AI

--
Attachment: workload-sample-202805.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hsu <ops@nebula.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <contracts@nebula.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exception request — batched inference failover and credits

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the extra context. We can accommodate a specialized carveout for scheduled DR exercises and propose a dual-tranche credit framework that separates availability and throughput degradation. I attached a clean draft of the SLA amendment and a tracked-redline to show the changes. High-level proposal below: 

1) Uptime baseline: 99.9% per calendar month; monthly service credits applied if monthly uptime falls below tiers (structured table in attachment).
2) Throughput tranche: separate metric measured as 95th-percentile tokens/sec over daily windows, with a remedial credit if throughput falls below a workload-specific baseline by >20% for >60 minutes.
3) DR exercise carveout: up to 6 hours/month scheduled per region with 72h advance notice; not eligible for credits.
4) Credit cap: aggregate monthly credits capped at 30% of that month's invoice; individual tranche caps defined per attachment.

Couple of notes: we generally resist unlimited carveouts or very low credit caps; the 30% cap is meant to preserve commercial balance while acknowledging higher batch sensitivity. Marissa — looping you in for legal/ops sanity checks.

If this direction looks reasonable I can circulate for Priya to mark commercial redlines and then produce a DocuSign packet.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priya Rao <contracts@nebula.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exception request — batched inference failover and credits

Ben / Tom — quick operational/legal perspective:

- The dual-tranche idea is solid; it maps to how we instrument serving (availability monitors vs throughput probes). We'll need to define measurement windows and probe placement in the attachment to avoid metric gaming.
- Suggest tightening the notice window for DR exercises to 48h (rather than 72h) with a requirement to schedule outside of business-critical daily windows where feasible.
- On credit caps: 30% aggregate is acceptable for pilot customers, but for renewals we prefer a 20% long-term cap with an option to expand based on committed capacity. Can note this as a time-bound concession (first 12 months).

I attached a short appendix template for metric definitions and a sample monitoring placement diagram. If Nebula agrees to the 48h notice and the 12-month pilot cap, we can mark the redlines.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: sla-metrics-appendix-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Tom Hsu <ops@nebula.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <contracts@nebula.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exception request — batched inference failover and credits

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the appendix. A few clarifications from our procurement/ops review: 

- We can accept a 48h notice for scheduled DR drills.
- We'd like the uptime baseline raised to 99.95% for the hosted endpoints that carry our real-time traffic (the batch jobs can remain under 99.9% baseline if you prefer). The reason is contractual downstream SLAs we have with our customers where sub-99.95% availability triggers penalties.
- On the credit cap: we'll accept the 12-month pilot at 30% but request an explicit review at renewal to consider a lower cap tied to committed spend.

If you can produce a redlined doc with the per-endpoint baseline distinction (real-time endpoints 99.95%, batch endpoints 99.9%) and the throughput tranche language, we'll route to legal. Priya will lead the contract-side redlines.

Appreciate the collaboration — Tom

Tom Hsu
Head of Platform Operations
Nebula AI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SLA exception request — batched inference failover and credits

Tom / Priya — appreciate the clarity. We updated the draft to include:
- Endpoint-specific uptime baselines: 99.95% for designated real-time endpoints; 99.9% for batch endpoints.
- Throughput tranche definitions and measurement windows (95th-percentile tokens/sec; remedial credit trigger: >20% degradation for >60 minutes).
- DR drill carveout at 6h/month per region with 48h notice.
- Pilot credit cap at 30% for the first 12 months with an automatic renewal discussion prompt 90 days before contract anniversary.

I've uploaded the redlined packet and started a DocuSign envelope for signatures (link below). Priya — once you complete commercial markups we'll finalize and issue. If Nebula agrees to baseline split and pilot cap terms, we should be able to execute within 10 business days.
